title: questlog conflicts.json
description: OPTIONAL per-roadmap record of COLLIDING WRITES that were HELD. Founder ruling, 2026-08-27: when two writers change the same record, the app must not keep whichever landed last. The second change is held — applied to nothing and discarded by nothing — and surfaces as a decision showing BOTH versions for the founder to rule on. While a hold is open the FIRST write stands as current, so the board stays readable rather than frozen. A warning shown after the loss is not a decision, it is a receipt. Lives at <projectRoot>/.questlog/conflicts.json alongside roadmap.json. Absent file = nothing has ever collided here (normal). Present file is validated strictly. schemaVersion stays 1 (back-compatible: old dirs load fine). Kept a SEPARATE file so roadmap.json's strict schema is untouched and no record ever carries a contested marker.

version.description: A record version: the first 12 hex chars of sha1(JSON.stringify(record)), derived at READ time and stored on no record anywhere. It beats updatedAt because it also catches a hand edit that forgot to bump one, and because decisions carry no updatedAt at all.

id.description: REQUIRED. "cf-" + 8 hex chars from the generator; any lowercase id slug validates.

ts.description: REQUIRED. When the change was held.

status.description: REQUIRED. "open" = waiting on a founder ruling (the first write is what renders). "ruled" = the founder decided; `ruling` says which way. "void" = the target was deleted, so there was nothing left to rule on; `voidReason` says so.

targetType.description: REQUIRED. Which kind of record was contested.

targetId.description: REQUIRED. The contested record. While the conflict is OPEN this id must still exist on the road — a delete voids its holds rather than leaving them dangling (validate.mjs enforces this; term targets are exempt because it collects no term ids).

source.description: REQUIRED. Which surface the held write came in through.

actor.description: REQUIRED. Who made the held write.

action.description: REQUIRED. The tool name or ui_* action that was held (milestone_set_status, ui_unclear_set, ui_item_delete, …).

sessionId.description: OPTIONAL. The AI session that made the held write.

baseVersion.description: REQUIRED. The version the held writer was working from.

currentVersion.description: REQUIRED. The version that was actually on disk — the reason this is a collision at all.

current.description: REQUIRED. The WHOLE record as it stood: the write that landed FIRST, and what the board keeps rendering while the hold is open.

proposed.description: REQUIRED. The WHOLE record the held write would have produced, or null for a held DELETE (which proposes no record). Applying a ruling of keep:"held" writes this over the record entirely — that is what the founder was shown side by side.

input.description: REQUIRED. The raw call that was held, minus sessionId and baseVersion (attribution, not part of the argument). A held delete is re-run from this at ruling time, against today's road.

ruling.description: PRESENT IFF status is "ruled". The founder's decision, and nobody else's — an agent records it, never makes it.

keep.description: "current" = the first write stands. "held" = the held version was written over the record.

by.description: Who entered the ruling. It is the founder's call either way; an agent entering it is recording what they were told.

voidReason.description: PRESENT IFF status is "void". Why there is nothing left to rule on — "target deleted" is the only reason today.
